statement.p: A town has 4100 registered residents. Among them, there are 1476 Democrats and 1312 Republicans. The rest are Independents. What percentage of registered voters in this town are Independents?
In this town, of all registered voters are Independents.

solution.p: Out of 4100 registered voters, there are 1476 Democrats and 1312 Republicans. This implies there are 4100-1476-1312=1312 Independents.
Now this problem can be boiled down to this question: 1312 is what percent of 4100? We will show multiple methods to solve this problem.
We will use proportion to solve this problem.
Assume 1312 is x\% of 4100, so x out of 100 corresponds to 1312 out of 4100.
We will write and solve the proportion:
In this town, 32\% of all registered voters are Independents.
We will use the percentage formula to solve this problem.
This translation from English to may should help you remember the percentage formula.
Assume 1312 is x (as a percent) of 4100. We have:
In this town, 32\% of all registered voters are Independents.
In the sentence 1312 is what percent of 4100,

li.p: 4100 is the base (following the word of).

solution.p: By the formula \text{rate} = \frac{\text{percentage}}{\text{base}}, we do a division to solve the problem:
In this town, 32\% of all registered voters are Independents.
